written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385), read by section; page numbers are not cited (the manual was not open in the authoring environment, so no page was invented): the DD statement's DSNAME parameter (temporary datasets &&name, NULLFILE, omitted DSNAME), DUMMY, DISP (defaults, PASS), SYSOUT, OUTPUT, and 'Concatenating datasets'; the JOB statement's MSGCLASS; the EXEC COND parameter. The expected answers were written before any evaluator ran on them.
scenario_input: msgclass (optional): the JOB statement's MSGCLASS, read by hand. given: per step that starts, {rc: n} or {abend: code}.
scenario_answer: expect: per STEP.DDNAME of each step that runs: {datasets: [...]} in read order, {dummy: true}, {temporary: 'system-named'} or {dd_class, output?}. temporaries: per &&name its creating DD, the DDs that receive it and the step after which it is deleted ('JOB' = at the end of the job).
flow_jcl: //* #8413 slice 5: data flow between steps. What each DD of a step that
//* runs names (temporaries passed, DUMMY / NULLFILE, concatenations in
//* read order, SYSOUT classes and OUTPUT references). The answers are
//* in scenarios.json, written from IBM's z/OS MVS JCL Reference
//* (SA23-1385) before any evaluator ran on them.

scenarios.basis: DSNAME, temporary datasets (&&name), and DISP: S1 creates &&SORTED with DISP=(NEW,PASS), so the system keeps it and passes it to a later step that refers to it. S2 receives it with DISP=(OLD,PASS) and passes it on; S3 receives it with DISP=(OLD,DELETE), so it is deleted when S3 ends. S1's WORK DD names no dataset and asks for space: the system names a temporary dataset for it (DSNAME, 'if you omit DSNAME for a new dataset').

DISP defaults: a NEW dataset with no normal disposition is deleted at the end of its step, so &&GONE (a DSN with no DISP is NEW) is deleted after T1 and nobody receives it. &&KEPT is passed by T1; T2 and T3 code no normal disposition for an OLD / SHR dataset, which (ASSUMED A1) leaves the passed dataset passed, so T3 still gets it. A temporary dataset is deleted when the job ends, so its last stop is the end of the job.

EXEC COND=(4,LT,B1): B1 ended with 8, 4 < 8 is true, so B2 is bypassed. A bypassed step allocates none of its DDs: &&LOST is never created and B2's DUMMY DD does not exist. B3 runs and its SYSOUT=A DD names class A.

DD DUMMY: no dataset is allocated, a read gets end of file and a write is discarded. DSNAME=NULLFILE has the same effect as DUMMY. On a DD that codes DUMMY the other parameters (here DSN=PAY.REAL and DISP=(NEW,CATLG)) are checked for syntax and ignored, so PAY.REAL is not created or cataloged.

Concatenating datasets: a DD with a ddname followed by DD statements with no name is one logical dataset, read in the order the statements are coded; the same datasets coded in another order (M2.IN) are read in that other order. A concatenation is per step: M1.IN and M2.IN are different DDs. A GDG generation is a member like any other and keeps its relative number as coded.

Two temporaries passed by two steps and received in one concatenation: K3 reads &&PART2 first, then &&PART1 (coded order, not creation order). Each is received by K3.IN, and each DD's DISP=(OLD,DELETE) deletes its own dataset after K3.

SYSOUT: the first element is the output class; SYSOUT=* is the class of the JOB statement's MSGCLASS (X here); the second and third elements (writer, form) are not the class. OUTPUT=*.name names an OUTPUT statement (ASSUMED A2: the one in the same step, else the job-level one) and *.stepname.name one in that earlier step, so ONE uses OUT1, TWO uses OUT1 and OUT2 (R1's), LATE uses R1's OUT2. 'dd_class' is the class the DD itself codes: which class wins when the OUTPUT statement also codes CLASS is not answered (see refused).

assumed.text: DISP on a DD that receives a passed dataset with no normal disposition (DISP=OLD / SHR): the dataset stays passed. IBM's text for the default of an existing dataset was not at hand; this is the documented PASS continuation as recalled, so it is assumed, not cited.
OUTPUT=*.name resolves to an OUTPUT statement in the same step first, then to a job-level one. IBM's text on the referback forms was not at hand for the job-level case.

refused.construct: a temporary dataset received before any step creates it, or after it was deleted, or whose creator was bypassed
refused.why: a JCL error at allocation, not a data-flow answer

refused.construct: a temporary dataset with a CATLG / UNCATLG / KEEP disposition
refused.why: IBM's treatment of a retained &&name is not answered here

refused.construct: DUMMY coded on a DD inside a concatenation
refused.why: which datasets of the concatenation remain is not answered here

refused.construct: SYSOUT with no class (SYSOUT=(,)) or SYSOUT=* with no MSGCLASS given
refused.why: the class would come from an OUTPUT statement's CLASS or the installation default, not carried by the rows

refused.construct: an OUTPUT reference that names no OUTPUT statement of the job
refused.why: a JCL error, not a data-flow answer

refused.construct: the class a SYSOUT DD gets when its OUTPUT statement also codes CLASS
refused.why: which one wins is not answered here; 'dd_class' is the DD's own
